findings:
- id: JEV-001
  severity: high
  category: data/authority flow
  description: The durable-pending order is internally inconsistent for projection failures and underspecified for the single-candidate path.
  evidence: Section 6.1 records running only after projection and candidate generation, but also requires projection/input errors to become recovery_required for the same decision. Section 4.2 skips the remote call for one candidate without explicitly stating whether pending/proposedAction and crash reconciliation still apply.
  required_fix: Specify one transaction sequence covering all paths: establish decision identity, durably record or deterministically create recovery state around every fallible projection step, and route single-candidate execution through proposedAction, expect-version, atomic transition, and crash reconciliation without an HTTP call.
- id: JEV-002
  severity: high
  category: lifecycle
  description: closure_unconfirmed has no defined convergence path while the owning process remains alive.
  evidence: After the 2-second grace, retry, new games, lock release, and successful stop are prohibited. Recovery requires verified owner death, but the design does not define whether a later-settling request can complete disposal or which component terminates the wedged owner after requestStop returns an error.
  required_fix: Define a terminal escalation contract. Either allow late settlement to transition closure_unconfirmed to safely disposed while capability remains revoked, or require a specified supervisor/operator action to terminate the owner and document how a new process validates death and adopts the stale lock.
- id: JEV-003
  severity: medium
  category: privacy
  description: Authority and disclosure for transmitting online participants’ gameplay telemetry are incomplete.
  evidence: The projection sends pseudonymized public seats and prior human actions, but the remote-processing notice is specified only on the lobby runtime selector. No equivalent participant join/table disclosure or established host authority rule is defined.
  required_fix: Add participant-visible disclosure before play, or explicitly document the product authority under which the host enables pseudonymized transmission for all seats. Keep names and stable participant identifiers excluded as designed.

- P3 installed-SDK and bounded live-contract gates, including abort beyond the grace period and eventual late settlement.
- P4 crash/race tests for projection failure, single-candidate execution, proposedAction boundaries, stop/response races, and duplicate retry.
- P5 privacy canaries across host, participant, SSE, summary, replay, export, logs, and app snapshots.

- Actual latency, usage, and strategy quality do not block readiness and are correctly excluded from GTO or performance claims.
- Availability of an existing supervisor that can terminate and replace a closure_unconfirmed owner is unknown; this does block lifecycle readiness until JEV-002 is resolved.
